Title: Seeded DELIVERED order had an incomplete status-event history (no PENDING/PAID/SHIPPED events)
Environment: Seed script against SQLite, Windows 11, Node 24.21.0
StepsToReproduce:
1. npm run db:reset (seed the database)
2. Run the SQL check DB-22: look for orders without an initial PENDING event
3. Inspect the order_events rows of the seeded order ORD-00002
ExpectedResult: Every order has a complete status history (PENDING -> PAID -> SHIPPED -> DELIVERED) so that order history and audit views are truthful.
ActualResult: ORD-00002 (DELIVERED) had exactly one event (from_status NULL, to_status DELIVERED); the earlier transitions were missing.
RootCause: app/server/src/seed.js inserted a single event using the order's final status instead of replaying the transition chain.
RetestResult: PASS - DB-22 now reports 0 orders missing the initial PENDING event; the API event tests also pass.
RegressionResult: PASS - full SQL suite 23/23, API suite 72/72 after the fix.
Rationale: Fixed at the source (seed replayed the full chain). The failing run was preserved as evidence before the fix, as required for honest reporting.

Title: Malformed JSON request body returned HTTP 500 instead of 400
Environment: ShopSure API on Windows 11, Node 24.21.0, Express 4.21.2
StepsToReproduce:
1. Send POST /api/auth/login with a truncated JSON body: {"email": "a@example.com", 
2. Observe the HTTP status and response body
ExpectedResult: 400 with `{ error: { code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' } }` - a client error for a client mistake.
ActualResult: 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` because body-parser's SyntaxError is not an HttpError and fell through to the generic 500 branch.
RootCause: errorHandler() in app/server/src/lib/errors.js only understood HttpError instances.
RetestResult: PASS - same request now returns 400 VALIDATION_ERROR; recorded in the re-run of the manual session.
RegressionResult: PASS - API suite 72/72, Postman 76/76 assertions after the fix.
Rationale: Fixed by mapping body-parser error types (entity.parse.failed, entity.too.large, encoding.unsupported) to correct 4xx responses. Client mistakes must never look like server faults.

Title: Oversized request body returned HTTP 500 instead of 413
Environment: ShopSure API on Windows 11, Node 24.21.0, Express 4.21.2, body limit 100kb
StepsToReproduce:
1. Send POST /api/auth/login with a ~200 KB JSON body
2. Observe the HTTP status and response body
RootCause: Same as SHOP-BUG-002: body-parser's entity.too.large error was not translated.
RetestResult: PASS - the same request now returns 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE.
RegressionResult: PASS - API suite and Postman run repeated without failures.
Rationale: Fixed together with SHOP-BUG-002 by adding explicit body-parser error mapping.

Title: SEEDED: cart accepts more units than the product has in stock
Environment: ShopSure with SEED_DEFECTS=1 (never active by default)
StepsToReproduce:
1. Start the server with SEED_DEFECTS=1
2. POST /api/cart/items with a quantity above the product stock
ActualResult: With the flag enabled the stock guard is skipped, so the line is accepted - exactly the failure the automation must catch.
RetestResult: PASS - with the flag off the same test passes, proving the detection is caused by the seeded defect and not by flakiness.
RegressionResult: N/A - legitimate runs keep the flag off.
Rationale: Kept as a permanent, reproducible ability to demonstrate defect detection. Fully documented in seeded-defects.md.

Title: SEEDED: cancelling an order does not restore product stock
StepsToReproduce:
1. Start the server with SEED_DEFECTS=1
2. Place an order, cancel it, then read the product stock again
ExpectedResult: Stock returns to its pre-order value (correct build behaviour).
ActualResult: With the flag enabled the stock restore is skipped, so stock stays reduced - inventory drifts downwards.
DetectedBy: tests/api/seeded-defects.spec.ts (SHOP-BUG-102 test) and the cancel regression test
RetestResult: PASS - with the flag off, stock is restored and the SQL stock checks stay green.
RegressionResult: N/A - legitimate runs keep the flag off.
Rationale: Demonstrates detection of a silent data-integrity defect that no user would notice immediately.

Title: SEEDED: minPrice filter is exclusive, dropping products priced exactly at the boundary
StepsToReproduce:
1. Start the server with SEED_DEFECTS=1
2. GET /api/products?minPrice=50 and look for products priced exactly 50.00
ExpectedResult: The 50.00 product is included (correct build behaviour).
ActualResult: With the flag enabled the comparison uses '>' so the 50.00 product disappears - a classic off-by-one boundary defect.
RetestResult: PASS - with the flag off the boundary test passes.
RegressionResult: N/A - legitimate runs keep the flag off.
Rationale: Boundary defects are easy to miss manually; this proves the declared boundary tests really execute at the edge.
